$note: HAND-CURATED overlay for the System Map (YED-232, docs/system-map.prd.md). The generator (scripts/gen-system-map.mjs) merges this with facts it derives from the pipeline repo — frontmatter descriptions, first-shipped dates, tools, the ADR-8 file graph — into src/data/system-map.json. Everything here is a judgement: `why.text` must cite its `why.source`; a `status` override must carry a `reason`; `reviewed_at` is when a human last checked the entry against the code (the generator flags entries whose files changed after that date). `toolsExclude` removes a tool the generator's whole-file mcp__ scan picks up from text that only forbids or disables it.

zones.blurb: Where an event enters the system — a calendar acceptance, not a form.

zones.blurb: The research and content engines. Claude skills do the thinking; the parent thread owns the fan-out.

zones.blurb: The Market-Intelligence Engine's system of record — one Postgres graph, claims first-class.

zones.blurb: Where the outputs live: Notion for content and research, HubSpot for people, Linear for what's open.

components.name: Going-to-Events calendar
components.summary: A dedicated Google Calendar. Accepting an event there is the pipeline's only trigger.

why.text: The predecessor project (new-jack-city) chained n8n → Claude → Notion and failed repeatedly at the integration layer. Take 3 separates 'do great research' from 'put it in the right places': the trigger is the moment Alex already performs — accepting an invite — and nothing is automated between that and a human reading the brief.

build.note: The predecessor's GCal intake (YED-6) was the one piece that worked; it became the intake model here.

why.text: Calendar-invite-as-structured-intake: Alex pastes a PIPELINE block into the invite at acceptance time, the command finds those events, dedups them against Notion and runs research + pre-event content per event with a continue-or-quit gate between them. Most real invites carry no block, so it also parses the raw description rather than exiting.

build.note: Validated end-to-end on Ray Dev Day, 2026-05-20.

components.name: Event claim
components.summary: A machine-global lock on an event's Notion namespace for the duration of a run.

why.text: Git worktrees isolate checkouts but not Notion. On 2026-09-20 two sessions ran the same event and disagreed on two facts; duplicate effort is cheap, contradictory records that later runs read as fact are not. So a run claims the event first (exit 3 = someone else holds it → go read-only), claims expire after 4h so a crashed run can't lock an event, and the run-close gates now key on the same claim to know a run is still in progress.

The core of the system: an invite goes in, a researched brief on the room comes out. It is one artifact with two layers (ADR-5): a scannable head for the room and a ~45-minute prose Deep Read for the commute. The fan-out — four specialists in parallel, then a synthesizer — runs from the parent thread because the Agent SDK does not let a subagent spawn subagents; designing around that constraint instead of fighting it is what made the pipeline reliable. Since YED-205 the research also writes its Evidence Ledger into the knowledge graph, so the next run compounds instead of restarting.

build.note: Monolithic skill (2026-04) → multi-agent rebuild (2026-05-04) → orchestrator-to-synthesizer pivot (2026-05-07) → Deep Read (2026-08) → graph write-back (2026-09-27).

why.text: Turns the brief into the first half of a deliberate two-part arc: a per-event LinkedIn post (three hook variants, every one shipped to Notion for comment-based iteration), a Sunday roundup that sets the table without taking a side, prepared questions, and 200-character connection-request notes rather than DMs (LinkedIn's free tier only messages 1st-degree connections). Stance is earned by space and expertise — a hot take in a synopsis is worth nothing — so the bold point of view is deferred to the post-event recap.
why.source: .claude/skills/pre-event-content/SKILL.md; .claude/references/content-style-guide.md v0.5–0.9; CLAUDE.md § Phase 2 (DM rule 2026-05-20, stance rule 2026-05-30)

build.note: Steering-interview (Aim → Sharpen) added 2026-05-30 so Alex's angle is captured before generation, not corrected after.

why.text: The second half of the arc: what was actually said, cashed against the pre-event setup. A transcript (a Supercut recording preferred; an audio file through ElevenLabs Scribe or a manual paste as fallbacks) is conditioned into a quote bank, synthesized into a post_event_brief — the canonical store every downstream draft references — then drafted by the content-correspondent skill. Since ADR-10 it also creates the attended event row in the graph and attaches the pre-event claims to it.

build.note: Granola auto-fetch built then disabled 2026-05-27; recording ingest + slide alignment added 2026-09.

components.name: Voice & visual system
components.summary: The style guide, anti-patterns, audience north star, shared content patterns (including goal tagging, graded later by the tag-outcome skill) and the visual-brief spec every content skill imports.

why.text: Voice is a living system, not a prompt: Alex reviews drafts as inline Notion comments, and the update-voice-and-style skill mines those comments back into the guides so every skill inherits the correction once. Visuals must add information (architecture, comparison, progression) and never re-print the post; they are authored by Claude as self-contained HTML/SVG and exported to a 4:5 PDF — Gamma was removed on 2026-08-07 because it re-interpreted content and broke labels.

build.note: v0.5 (stance + self, 2026-05-30) → v0.6 (no I-led openers, 2026-08-07) → v0.9 (table-set context first, 2026-09-09).

why.text: Milestone 1 of the Market-Intelligence Engine and the first job-search consumer of the graph: a four-axis dossier (company, role, stage, interviewer) built by the same specialist fan-out and scored against a dossier rubric before it is written. It exists because the research engine is lens-agnostic, so the graph that preps an event can prep an interview. In use it has been thin: one run, and a write path that predates the one-write-path rule (ADR-9).

status.reason: Built and run once in 30 days; the dossier-synthesizer agent has never been dispatched, and Step 5 writes the graph with raw PostgREST upserts instead of the guarded spine_client path. The interview lens (YED-207) and ICP wiring (YED-152) are open.

components.name: /scan-roles (role radar)
components.summary: /scan-roles — pulls roles from public ATS boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable), dedupes on the ATS job id, scores them against Alex's target-role profile, lands them in a Notion Roles DB and mirrors each approved role into the graph as a role-posted event.

why.text: The job-search radar, and since YED-149 (2026-09-27) the graph's busiest producer: role postings are most of the graph's event rows. Every approved role lands as a role-posted event keyed only by its Notion page, so a rescan writes nothing new, and it waited until the Notion side had proved its dedup across five scans before touching the shared graph. The trend and voice scanners that used to share this box were retired in the 2026-09-28 reset.

Gmail is a first-class signal source (ADR-7): newsletters and event correspondence are the earliest, cheapest market signal Alex already receives. The miner reads an allowlist of senders, dedups on canonical URL, writes email signals to the graph through the one write path, and labels what it has processed. A denylist keeps private correspondence out by construction.

status.reason: Works, but dormant: one run to date and the last graph write was 2026-09-10. The Notion Companies mirror (YED-194) is still open.

components.name: Document knowledge base

status.reason: /ingest-doc and /ask-library work as manual commands, but the library holds 2 documents and 0 claims and neither command ran in the last 30 days (roadmap: 'value unproven'). Claim extraction into the ADR-10 claim table is not wired (YED-235).

components.summary: /ingest-doc and /ask-library — long documents (books, papers) archived to R2, chunked, embedded locally and stored in Supabase pgvector so they can be queried.

why.text: Large documents live outside the repos (the Knowledge Library) with R2 as the archive of record; ingesting them lets research cite primary sources instead of search snippets. It earns its keep only when the library's claims reach the pipelines, which is the unbuilt half.

components.name: Postgres knowledge graph
components.summary: One Supabase project (Empire prod) holding people, companies, topics, events, documents and claims — the system of record for market intelligence.

why.text: The 'no Supabase' rule held for the base pipeline, but a lens-agnostic intelligence engine needs a graph that persists across runs: an event is a hyperedge that connects people, companies and topics, and every run should compound what the last one learned. Consolidated onto this one project (ADR-1/ADR-4) after the separate GTM spine was decommissioned; accessed over REST with a scoped key, and through the Supabase MCP only for read-only inspection.
why.source: docs/adr/ADR-1-data-layer.md; docs/adr/ADR-4-increment-2.md; CLAUDE.md § measurement layer (tombstone re-scoped 2026-06-28); memory 2026-09-17 Supabase MCP canonical

build.note: Cutover 2026-08-10 (Increment 2b); gtm spine decommissioned; nightly health-check watches coherence.

why.text: Every write to the graph goes through one Python client that hard-fails on contact PII (ADR-9: email and phone never enter the spine — HubSpot holds contact detail). A single chokepoint is cheaper to audit than a Postgres constraint today and can become one later. It also carries the bounded retry that a live run exposed on 2026-09-27, when an intermittent network stall looked like a broken pipeline. The same run exposed the cause: about one in ten fresh network connections from the build machine stalls, so the client now reuses one connection for calls that are safe to repeat and retries anything that failed before it was sent — a 200-role run went from 24 minutes to under one.

ADR-10 makes claims first-class: a sourced, tiered statement ('web-verified', 'email-signal') attached to the entities it is about, with documents generalized so a research brief, a transcript and a newsletter are the same kind of thing. One producer library stages them; identity merges are human-only soft merges with a revert path. The A/B against the legacy retrieval showed the substrate wins on material and the legacy path on packaging, so both stay and the merge is the next step, not a rerun.
why.source: docs/adr/ADR-10-knowledge-substrate.md (Accepted 2026-09-27, Amendment 1); memory 2026-09-24 A/B verdict; memory 2026-09-27 identity S1b-lite

components.name: retrieve (lenses)
components.summary: The one retrieval interface: a lens (event · interview · content) plus seed entities in, a budgeted Context Pack of prior occasions, returning faces and scored claims out.

why.text: Consumers should never query tables directly; a lens names what a consumer needs and the interface enforces a token budget and a loud failure (exit 5) when the graph holds claims for these entities but the pack kept none — silent emptiness is how prior knowledge quietly stops compounding. The event lens is live; interview and content lenses are the open consumer work. The job lens is kept out of it on purpose: role postings never appear among an event's prior occasions (hundreds of them would crowd out the handful that matter); a seed company gets one hiring count line instead, and applications and interviews appear nowhere.

components.name: Topic intelligence

status.reason: The topic_intelligence tables have not been recomputed since the 2026-08-10 cutover: the nightly recompute was never wired (pg_cron not installed), the health-check went red for 9 nights into GitHub issues nobody read, and the Hub's trend panel served 7-week-old data. YED-230.

components.summary: Relevance scoring and topic movement over the graph — what is moving, for whom.

why.text: The graph is only useful if something ranks it: relevance per lens and movement per topic are what the Hub's planned topic-intelligence panels (YED-114) and the P2 architecture lens read. It is listed stale on purpose — this is the exact failure the map exists to make visible.

components.name: Notion (Content + Research Hub)
components.summary: Six bidirectionally-related databases: Events, People, Companies, Topics, Content Drafts, Project Ideas.

why.text: Notion is the review surface: Alex reads briefs and drafts there and comments inline, and those comments are mined back into the voice system. Page bodies hold long-form text, properties hold what must be filterable, and writes are dependency-ordered because relation fields need the URLs of pages created first. claude.ai MCP connectors are not available inside subagents, so every Notion write runs inline in the command's own (parent) thread; the notion-writer agent file is still in the repo but it is not the write path.
why.source: .claude/references/notion-schema.md; .claude/references/notion-write-gotchas.md; CLAUDE.md rule 5 (MCP writes run in the parent thread); hub-system-audit 2026-09-28 §2 (1,644 inline Notion MCP calls vs 2 notion-writer dispatches in 30 days)

build.note: Schema verified via MCP 2026-04-09; gotchas (a)–(m) accumulated from live failures.

components.name: HubSpot CRM
components.summary: Companies and Contacts with associations; event tracking as Notes because Static Lists are not writable over MCP.

why.text: HubSpot is where contact detail lives — the PII boundary (ADR-9) keeps email and phone out of the graph precisely because the CRM already holds them. Contacts are created only after Alex approves a confirmation table (judgement load keeps that step manual). A CRM replacement (Clarify) was evaluated and rejected on 2026-09-09.
why.source: CLAUDE.md § HubSpot Write Orchestration; docs/adr/ADR-9-pii-boundary.md; memory 2026-09-09 CRM + capture decision

components.name: Gmail
components.summary: Correspondence and newsletters — read as prior knowledge before research, mined as a signal source, labeled after processing.

why.text: The inbox already receives the market: newsletters, organizer emails, follow-ups. Reading it before research (Step 1.7) and mining it on a schedule (ADR-7) turns that into graph signals without a scraper. Write scope was granted narrowly (labels only) on 2026-09-10.

components.name: Linear
components.summary: The single source of truth for what is open. The build path on this map reads it live.

why.text: A static priorities block in the project instructions drifted the moment it was written, so Linear became the only place issue state lives and a SessionStart hook pulls the top priorities into every session. When git and Linear disagree, git is the fact and Linear gets corrected. Parked and deferred thoughts must be filed the same turn they are written — no 'revisit later' text without a pointer.

components.name: Build-quality judge
components.summary: /judge-build — one Sonnet reviewer, run on demand when an artifact class calls for it (a new skill or command, large code, a guarded path). It scores build-quality@6, flags rather than gates, and Alex is asked only on a flag.

why.text: Quality had to become a measurable signal, not a vibe. The judge grew from one reviewer to three seats (Sonnet voting, Gemini advisory, OpenAI shadow) with a quorum merge and a per-seat trust ladder, and the extra seats did not earn their keep: Gemini's '83% agreement' was its always-pass baseline (κ 0.14), the OpenAI seat stayed in shadow, and the quorum escalated on its own bundle mechanics. YED-231 (2026-09-28) cut it back to one reviewer whose verdict informs and never blocks.
why.source: .claude/references/judge.md; .claude/skills/judge-build/SKILL.md; memory 2026-09-19 judge seats + calibration; Linear YED-231

build.note: Rubric @1 (2026-06) → @3 (2026-07-17, calibration gate crossed) → three seats (2026-09-20) → @6 (2026-09-27) → one reviewer (2026-09-28, YED-231).

components.name: System graph (ADR-8)
components.summary: A derived graph over the repo's own build artifacts — every skill, command, agent, hook, ADR and note as a node, every load-bearing reference as an edge. Rebuilt by hand with build_graph.py (its session hooks are no longer registered); it is the source of this map's file layer.

why.text: Drift detection needs a substrate: when a reference points at a file that no longer exists, or a plan names a script that was never written, that should be mechanical fact surfaced at session start, not something a reviewer happens to notice. The graph is derived and gitignored — never hand-edited — so it cannot itself drift from the repo.

build.note: Increment 1 live; the session-start/stop hooks were unregistered in the 2026-09-28 reset, so the graph is rebuilt by hand before regenerating this map.

components.name: Operating rules
components.summary: The project instructions, the workflow manual, the platform-constraints registry, the git and PR conventions (spec before code, a linked Linear issue, one adversarial pass) and the build-in-public policy.

why.text: A memory-less agent needs its invariants where it will read them: which MCP account is which, what a subagent cannot do, why two sessions must never share a checkout, what may be public. Constraints have one home (platform-constraints.md) with memory files carrying pointers, and the reconciliation of branches is a role one session plays, not a habit everyone half-keeps.

components.name: Empire State Hub
components.summary: This site: a public build-in-public surface with two lenses (editorial and technical) and a small private /ops cockpit over Notion — events, entities, content and content performance.

why.text: Read-only, honesty-first, PII-safe by mechanical check. It exists to be the interview artifact — the place a hiring manager sees the system and the reasoning, not a résumé line. The private /ops side was cut from eleven dashboards to four on 2026-09-28: the rigor, market-intel, toolbox, backlog, ideas and learning-path views were an audience of one reading what Notion and Linear already render. The repos are public by design; personal files are gitignored and a check fails the build on any contact-PII field.
why.source: Linear project Empire State Hub; scripts/verify-public-safe.mjs; memory 2026-09-16 public repos, private data

components.name: Build journal & arcs
components.summary: A generator that turns git history and the per-session shards of the one wired project hook (a build-session Stop hook, gitignored) into the Hub's /journal, with a hand-written prose sidecar at break points. Run by hand or via /journal-entry.

why.text: The facts of the build should instrument themselves (YED-119) so the journal never depends on remembering to write; the prose — what a shipped PR meant — is a deliberate human-authored layer added at each break point, and its lapses are tracked as data.
why.source: memory: public build journal at break points; .claude/scripts/build_journal.py
